rv.q: Like life and politics, Sahota’s play is messy but it’s a bracingly vibrant debut and I absolutely loved it.
This deliciously vicious satire from Shaan Sahota – in her first fully staged drama – pulls no punches.
Certainly his creepingly explosive turn in Shaan Sahota’s debut drama is unmissable.

It’s a great idea, splicing political comedy and family drama together to pointed effect, and though the play struggles somewhat under the weight of its own ambition — a little like its characters — it’s delivered with a deliciously nasty flourish by Daniel Raggett’s cast.
But Sahota covers so much terrain that Daniel Raggett’s production sometimes stumbles when the mood shifts and the piece becomes hobbled in terms of plausibility by its plot-motoring twists.
The Estate is a play that’s full of such powerful emotional beats, without ever becoming a cohesive whole.
It feels like two different shows crashing into one another, bound only by a corrosive skepticism about politicians.
The shouting and the fighting are as synthetic as the soundbites.
THE ESTATE runs 2hours 20mins (with interval) and is heartily recommended.
It’s uneven, yet relentlessly arresting. Sahota must be commended for her ambition here – the landing may not be perfect, but the sequence of flourishes certainly wows.
When all its pieces fall into place, it is poignant and absolutely hilarious.
The evening is bright with a kind of furious fun which hides most of its shortcomings.
There are far too many threads here, poorly orchestrated.

The two halves don't always gel, and there are sharp changes in tone, veering suddenly from farce to tragedy, from hilarity to shock – but for the most part it works in an entertaining rollercoaster of emotions boosted by a riveting lead performance from Adeel Akhtar.

cn.t: Sahota's debut play blends political satire with family drama to mixed results, with an uneven structure that doesn't always gel. Akhtar's explosive performance anchors this provocative, wildly funny yet flawed exploration of race and ambition.
